questions.stem: The Preamble to the Indian Constitution begins with which words?
questions.explanation: The Preamble OPENS with 'WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC...' This echoes the opening of the US Constitution ('We the People'). 'WE THE PEOPLE' emphasises POPULAR SOVEREIGNTY — the Constitution derives its authority from the people, not from any monarch or external power. The Preamble was LAST TO BE ADOPTED by the Constituent Assembly (on 26 November 1949), after all articles were finalised. It was AMENDED ONCE (42nd Amendment, 1976) — adding SOCIALIST, SECULAR, and INTEGRITY. Ends with: '...HEREBY ADOPT, ENACT AND GIVE TO OURSELVES THIS CONSTITUTION.' Based on Jawaharlal Nehru's OBJECTIVES RESOLUTION (13 Dec 1946), adopted by Constituent Assembly on 22 Jan 1947. Preamble is the KEY to the Constitution (K.M. Munshi), reflects its 'soul and spirit' (Thakurdas Bhargava).

questions.stem: The OBJECTIVES RESOLUTION — which later became the Preamble in slightly modified form — was moved in the Constituent Assembly by:
questions.explanation: OBJECTIVES RESOLUTION — moved by JAWAHARLAL NEHRU on 13 DECEMBER 1946 in the Constituent Assembly. Adopted unanimously on 22 JANUARY 1947. It outlined the key vision of the future Indian Constitution: (1) India as a SOVEREIGN INDEPENDENT REPUBLIC; (2) Territories of British India + Indian States acceding to form a UNION; (3) All powers derived from the PEOPLE; (4) Guaranteed rights including Justice (social/economic/political), Equality, Freedom (of thought, expression, belief, faith, worship, vocation, association), Fraternity, + safeguards for minorities, backward classes, tribes; (5) Maintenance of territorial integrity; (6) Contribution to world peace + welfare of mankind. This became the philosophical foundation + is directly reflected in the PREAMBLE. The Constituent Assembly was ELECTED by Provincial Assemblies; first sat 9 Dec 1946; adopted Constitution 26 Nov 1949; it came into force 26 Jan 1950.

questions.stem: Which words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment (1976) during the Emergency?
questions.explanation: 42nd Amendment (1976) added THREE words to the Preamble: (1) 'SOCIALIST' — reflecting Indira Gandhi's policy direction (nationalisation of banks/coal; welfare state orientation); (2) 'SECULAR' — though the Constitution was already in practice secular, explicit mention added. Secularism here is the 'principled distance' from all religions (neither Indian nor French-style laïcité); (3) 'INTEGRITY' — added to the phrase 'unity and INTEGRITY of the Nation' (original: just 'unity'). All three were retained even after the 44th Amendment (1978) reversed many 42nd provisions. Today: 'SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC' in the Preamble. Kesavananda Bharati (1973) ruled the Preamble IS PART of the Constitution (reversing Berubari Union Case 1960 which said it was NOT). Thus, the Preamble CAN BE AMENDED (subject to basic structure doctrine).
questions.subject: Polity

_fixes.was: SOCIALIST, SECULAR, and INTEGRITY (of the Nation)

questions.stem: The Preamble guarantees its citizens JUSTICE — in which three forms?
questions.explanation: Preamble's exact phrasing on Justice: 'JUSTICE, social, economic and political'. These three forms: (1) SOCIAL — end of inequalities based on caste, colour, race, sex, religion; inspired by the Russian Revolution; manifest in reservations, abolition of untouchability (Art 17), protection of SC/ST/OBC/minorities. (2) ECONOMIC — ending economic inequalities; freedom from hunger, poverty, exploitation; reflected in DPSP (equal pay for equal work, right to work, living wages, distribution of wealth). (3) POLITICAL — universal adult franchise (18+), equal political rights, no discrimination in political participation, Article 326. All three derive from the RUSSIAN REVOLUTION of 1917 (via USSR Constitution's influence). The Preamble continues: 'LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; EQUALITY of status and of opportunity; and to promote among them all FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation'. Liberty/Equality/Fraternity from the French Revolution (1789).

questions.stem: The date mentioned in the Preamble — 'adopted, enacted and given to ourselves this constitution' on 26 NOVEMBER 1949 — is celebrated as:
questions.explanation: 26 NOVEMBER 1949 — the CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY ADOPTED the Constitution of India on this day. 26 November has been officially celebrated as CONSTITUTION DAY (Samvidhan Divas) in India since 2015 — notified by the Ministry of Social Justice, commemorating Dr. B.R. AMBEDKAR's 125th birth anniversary year (he was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee). Previously also called 'LAW DAY' by the Bar Council. DISTINCT from: (1) REPUBLIC DAY (26 January) — when the Constitution CAME INTO FORCE (1950); (2) INDEPENDENCE DAY (15 August) — partition + independence. Why 26 January chosen as Republic Day? To honour the 1929 Lahore session's PURNA SWARAJ declaration of 26 January 1930. Constitution came into force on 26 Jan 1950 — making India a REPUBLIC (no longer a Dominion under the British Crown). The Constitution originally had 395 ARTICLES, 22 PARTS, 8 SCHEDULES. Now (post amendments): ~470 articles, 25 parts, 12 schedules. since 2015; Samvidhan Divas.

questions.stem: Who is called the 'CHIEF ARCHITECT OF THE INDIAN CONSTITUTION' and was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee?
questions.explanation: Dr. BHIMRAO RAMJI AMBEDKAR (Baba Saheb, 1891-1956) — CHAIRMAN of the DRAFTING COMMITTEE (7 members, Aug 1947). Considered the CHIEF ARCHITECT of the Constitution. Other members of Drafting Committee: Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Mohammad Saadullah, B.L. Mitter (later replaced by N. Madhava Rau), D.P. Khaitan (died during term, replaced by T.T. Krishnamachari), N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar. Ambedkar was a remarkable jurist + economist + social reformer: born into Mahar (Dalit) community, overcame caste discrimination, earned PhD from Columbia Univ (first Indian) + London School of Economics + Bar-at-law from Gray's Inn. Champion of DEPRESSED CLASSES. Signed POONA PACT with Gandhi 1932. FIRST LAW MINISTER of independent India (1947-51). Converted to Buddhism (1956, Deekshabhoomi Nagpur) with 600,000 Dalits — founded NAVAYANA (Neo-Buddhist) movement. Awarded BHARAT RATNA posthumously in 1990. Wrote: Annihilation of Caste, Who Were the Shudras, Buddha and His Dhamma.

questions.stem: The illustrator of the ORIGINAL HANDWRITTEN MANUSCRIPT of the Indian Constitution (with calligraphic text + beautiful artwork) was:

options.option_text: Prem Behari Narain Raizada (calligraphy) + NANDALAL BOSE & Beohar Rammanohar Sinha

questions.explanation: ORIGINAL CONSTITUTION MANUSCRIPT — an exquisite handwritten document, 251 pages, no typos — was calligraphed in English by PREM BEHARI NARAIN RAIZADA (Delhi-based calligrapher, in flowing italic script over 6 months for a fee of nothing — he asked only to sign his name on every page). Illustrated / decorated by NANDALAL BOSE (principal of Kala Bhavana at Santiniketan, one of India's greatest artists) + BEOHAR RAMMANOHAR SINHA (one of Nandalal's disciples, who illustrated the Preamble page). Hindi version calligraphed by VASANT KRISHNA VAIDYA + illustrations by NANDALAL BOSE. The artwork features panels depicting Indian history + culture from Indus Valley through independence: Mohenjo-daro, Ramayana, Mahabharata, Buddha, Mahavira, Ashoka, Gupta court, Akbar's court, Shivaji, Rani Lakshmibai, Gandhi's Dandi March, Netaji + INA, refugee crossing, India's flag — a visual history. ORIGINAL MANUSCRIPT is preserved in helium-filled case in the Parliament House Library, Delhi.

questions.stem: The Preamble declares India as a 'REPUBLIC'. What does this specifically signify?

options.option_text: India is ruled by a monarch
The Head of State (President) is ELECTED (not hereditary) and holds office for a fixed term
India is a dominion of the British Commonwealth

questions.explanation: REPUBLIC = a form of government where the HEAD OF STATE is ELECTED (directly or indirectly), NOT HEREDITARY. India's President is INDIRECTLY ELECTED by an electoral college of MPs + MLAs for 5-year terms. Contrasts with a MONARCHY (hereditary king/queen — e.g., UK, Japan, Saudi Arabia). India was a DOMINION (under British Crown) from 15 Aug 1947 till 26 Jan 1950, when the Constitution came into force and India became a REPUBLIC. Other Preamble-defining terms: SOVEREIGN — independent, not subject to any external authority (not a dominion, not under the British monarch). DEMOCRATIC — government by the people, via free/fair elections, universal adult franchise, rule of law, independent judiciary. SOCIALIST — commitment to economic justice (added 1976). SECULAR — state has NO official religion, all religions equally treated (added 1976). The FULL DESCRIPTION: 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'.

questions.stem: The Indian Constituent Assembly took how long to frame the Constitution, how many sessions did it hold, and how many members did it have (after reorganisation post-Partition)?
questions.explanation: Constituent Assembly facts: DURATION — 9 December 1946 (first meeting) to 26 November 1949 (Constitution adopted) = 2 YEARS 11 MONTHS 18 DAYS (India's 'iconic period' cited in countless exams). TOTAL SESSIONS: 11. TOTAL SITTING DAYS: 166. ORIGINAL MEMBERS (pre-Partition): 389. POST-PARTITION (14 Aug 1947): 299 (members from Pakistan + some from princely states withdrew). Indirectly elected by Provincial Assemblies. COMPOSITION: 208 from INC + 73 from Muslim League + 18 others + 93 from Princely States. Chairman of CA: Dr. SACHIDANAND SINHA (Temporary, 1st session); Dr. RAJENDRA PRASAD (Permanent, from 11 Dec 1946). Chairman of DRAFTING COMMITTEE: Dr. B.R. AMBEDKAR. CONSTITUTIONAL ADVISOR: Sir B.N. RAU. Full Constitution had 395 Articles, 22 Parts, 8 Schedules at adoption. Sessions held at Constitution Hall (now Parliament House Central Hall). Meeting of CA Dec 9, 1946 with Sinha presiding.

questions.stem: 'The PREAMBLE IS A PART OF THE CONSTITUTION.' This was SETTLED LAW in which Supreme Court case?

options.option_text: Berubari Union Case (1960) — held Preamble NOT part of the Constitution
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) — reversed Berubari, held Preamble IS PART

questions.explanation: Evolution of the question 'Is the Preamble part of the Constitution?': (1) BERUBARI UNION CASE (1960 — 8-judge SC bench on India-Pakistan land cession to Pakistan): held Preamble is NOT a part of the Constitution — 'it is a key to the mind of the makers'. (2) KESAVANANDA BHARATI v. STATE OF KERALA (1973 — 13-judge bench, landmark Basic Structure Doctrine case): OVERRULED Berubari; held the Preamble IS PART of the Constitution AND can be amended (but basic structure cannot be destroyed). This remains the settled position. Thus the 42nd Amendment's additions to the Preamble (1976) were constitutionally valid. (3) LIC OF INDIA CASE (1995): reaffirmed Preamble as 'integral part'. Preamble is NOT enforceable in court (unlike articles), but is a KEY to interpreting ambiguous provisions. Preamble reflects the IDEALS / PHILOSOPHY / OBJECTIVES of the Constitution makers. Called the 'SOUL OF THE CONSTITUTION' by Thakurdas Bhargava, 'BIRTH CERTIFICATE OF THE CONSTITUTION' by K.M. Munshi.
